Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key clinical findings: Patient presents with acute onset of dry, red, itchy skin on hands and arms starting a few days after swimming, unresponsive to coconut butter, with no systemic symptoms; history notable for work stress and family history of atopy (asthma, hayfever); no prior personal skin conditions.  
- Working diagnosis: Irritant or allergic contact dermatitis (High likelihood), supported by symptom onset shortly after swimming, localization to exposed areas, and absence of systemic symptoms.  
- Additional considerations: New onset atopic dermatitis (Medium likelihood) given family history of atopy and stress as a potential trigger; xerosis due to environmental factors (Medium likelihood) as patient suspects weather but acute onset and prominent redness make pure xerosis less likely; irritant reaction to topical coconut butter less likely as symptoms preceded its use.  
- Management plan: Prescribe topical corticosteroid cream and emollients; consider over-the-counter oral antihistamines for itch; provide patient education leaflet on dermatitis; advise follow-up if symptoms persist or worsen.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Irritant or allergic contact dermatitis (High): Acute onset localized rash shortly after swimming; consistent with pool chemical exposure and typical presentation.  
- Atopic dermatitis (new onset) (Medium): Possible given family atopy history and stress, though no prior personal eczema and rash onset acute after swimming.  
- Xerosis (dry skin) due to environmental causes (Medium): Considered due to patient’s suspicion of weather impact; redness and acute onset less typical.
